intent: A host that did not win and a Games that was not yet the Games: medal bars make Norway's haul dwarf the host's three bronzes, a white flash marks the 1926 moment the week was renamed the first Winter Olympics, and a counter runs the athletes up to 258 over a pin on the town under the Alps.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country hosted the FIRST Winter Olympics?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country hosted the first Winter Olympics?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: France. A small ski town under the Alps, in 1924.

lines.direction: ease back so France and Switzerland share the frame; the Swiss flag-ball thinks on 'Switzerland'; three medal bars rise on 'Norway' with the host's bar a stub; the Norwegian flag-ball looks cool on 'medals' as France pulses
lines.text: Switzerland hosted the next ones. Norway sent the champions and went home with the most medals.

lines.direction: tighten on the Alps; a snowflake sticker on 'week'; a white flash and the 1926 card on 'movement'; the Chamonix pin and tag land on 'first' with a rings-style trophy sticker as France pulses
lines.text: It began as a winter sports week. Only in 1926 did the Olympic movement call it the first Winter Games.

lines.direction: hold close on the town; the athlete counter runs to 258 from 'nations' to 'women' with a skater sticker; the ONLY BRONZE card on 'bronze' as the French flag-ball grins anyway; pin leaves at the end
lines.text: 16 nations, 258 athletes, 11 of them women, and the host took home nothing but bronze.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A ski week became the Games. Follow us.
